clue.text: Perhaps in error about a painter's original version

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, that is around, the pieces that follow
something done in error is done wrongly, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps mistakenly, describes an early draft of an artist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is split around the inserted pieces, and "'s original" is only a link to the definition, though it reads as part of the painter's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A restatement of a text in other words is one rendering, or version, of it.

clue.text: Spirit in play requisite for fast-moving sport

explanation.surface: An item needed for a quick game in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: The first is the mischievous sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream; the second is the disc used in ice hockey.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shakespearean sprite shares the name with the rubber disc hit in ice hockey.

clue.text: Butterfly that may be caught in net

definitions.text: that may be caught in net

explanation.surface: A butterfly that a collector might trap.
explanation.walkthrough: The net is not a collector's but a hairnet, which holds a curl of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown butterfly bears this name, as does a long curl of hair held in a hairnet.

clue.text: Coward's acts a soldier survives

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
to survive is to live on

explanation.surface: A coward's behaviour is said to keep a soldier alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Coward is Noël Coward, the English playwright, and 'acts' means a play in acts, not deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a comedy in three acts by Noël Coward.

clue.text: A source of information, by the way

definitions.text: A source of information, by the way

parts.words: A source of information, by the way
parts.note: by the way reads as an aside, but literally means beside the road

explanation.surface: An offhand remark about where someone heard something.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside board tells motorists directions and distances.

clue.text: Decide to fix a bench

explanation.surface: Choosing to repair a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a matter is to resolve or agree on it, and the same word names a high-backed wooden seat.

clue.text: Victoria station, for example is not close to Maidenhead

parts.note: being not close to something is being far from it
the head of the word Maiden is its first letter, M

explanation.surface: A London rail terminus is said to be a long way from a Thames-side town.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is not the London terminus but the Australian state, where a station is a large sheep or cattle holding. Maidenhead is a town west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a station is a big agricultural holding, and Victoria is one of the states.

clue.text: Bishop's supportive about living

indicators.note: about says the word for supportive goes around the other piece

parts.note: aiding means helping, supportive
B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: A bishop is a source of support about life.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 's means 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to dwell or stay, so the adjective means remaining or dwelling.

clue.text: Modest start for this big name in music

definitions.text: Modest start for this big name in music

parts.words: Modest start for this big name in music
parts.note: Modest is not humble here but the Russian first name of a famous composer

explanation.surface: A celebrated musician had humble beginnings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Russian composer of Boris Godunov and Pictures at an Exhibition had the first name Modest.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer's full name begins with the forename Modest.

clue.text: Girlfriend's argument against poem repelled poet

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the poem's title is written backwards

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem
Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A woman's objection to a verse sends a poet packing.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman someone tells their secrets to is a close female friend; the clue's 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: Bent article put in again!

indicators.note: put in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: bis is a musical direction meaning again, repeat
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about an article being inserted once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent for something is an inclination or leaning, a predisposition.

clue.text: Successful player one left out of a silent film is distraught

indicators.note: distraught means upset and in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left, and only one of the two in the fodder

explanation.surface: A winning actor misses out on a silent picture and is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one L out of A SILENT FILM IS ('out of' links) and 'distraught' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who wins through to the penultimate round of a knockout has been successful.

clue.text: Wingless insect or fly, heard but not seen

indicators.note: heard but not seen means the word is only spoken, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: to fly is to run away, to flee

explanation.surface: A tiny bug, or a fly, is something you hear without spotting it.
explanation.definitionFit: This parasite is a jumping insect with no wings.

clue.text: Colours displayed here quite close to Magenta

definitions.text: Colours displayed here quite close to Magenta

parts.words: Colours displayed here quite close to Magenta
parts.note: military colours were carried at a battle fought in 1859 near the town of Magenta, and the battle's name is also a purplish-red dye close in shade to magenta

explanation.surface: A paint chart shows shades that are almost magenta.
explanation.walkthrough: Colours are regimental flags, and Magenta is a town in Lombardy that gave its name both to a battle and to a dye; the answer did likewise, a battle and a dye, a few weeks later.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian village gave its name to a battle of 1859 and to a reddish-purple aniline dye.

clue.text: Fielder covering empty space at very close range

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece covering the second sits above it

parts.note: point is a cricket fielding position, square on the off side
a blank is an empty space to be filled in

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder stands guard over a gap, very near the batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: POINT is a cricket fielding position near the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting from so close that aim hardly matters is firing from right up close.

clue.text: Eclipse what's not in fashion, say

parts.note: something that is not in is out

indicators.note: say means the next word is spoken, so a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: a fashion is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: To put something in the shade is to be unfashionable, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed in importance is to overshadow, to put in the shade.

clue.text: Frivolous girl almost finished champagne before concert

indicators.note: almost finished means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: fizz is slang for champagne
a gig is a pop concert

explanation.surface: A flighty young woman nearly drained the bubbly before a show.
explanation.definitionFit: This old word names a giddy, flirtatious young woman.

clue.text: Prince's not entirely shut a clumsy player up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a door not entirely shut is ajar
a ham is a bad, overacting player

explanation.surface: A prince keeps a door ajar for a poor actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AJAR + A + HAM as one run. The clue's 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian ruler of a princely state held this title, meaning great king.

clue.text: Intellectual taking notice? Egghead's knocked sideways

indicators.note: a word knocked sideways is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever person pays attention, and the egghead is staggered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked sideways' jumbles NOTICE; 'taking' and 'Egghead's' just dress the surface, with the egghead echoing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare adjective describes things of the mind or intellect.

clue.text: Mundane chance

explanation.surface: An ordinary opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is from 'not an earthly', meaning no chance at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly and down-to-earth for the first; in the idiom 'not an earthly' the word means a hope or prospect.

clue.text: Lizard — one lies with no end of patience in sun

indicators.note: in says the next pieces go inside the word for sun

parts.note: to sun oneself is to bask
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: with no says a letter is removed from the word before
the end of patience is its last letter

explanation.surface: A reptile stretches out patiently in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sun' is a verb here, not the star; 'with no end of patience' removes the last letter of patience, E, from the word for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical American reptile has a crest it can raise, named after the mythical serpent.

clue.text: Dye partly staining raincoat

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dye has partly marked a mac.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix colour deep into fibres is to dye them fast, the old sense of the verb.

clue.text: Convincing to a businessman

explanation.surface: Persuasive to someone in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: split businessman into business, CO for company, and man, GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasive argument is compelling; read cryptically, a company plus a gentleman spells the word.

clue.text: Save fifty in ocean off Port of Spain

parts.note: save in the sense of except is bar

indicators.note: off means the letters are spoiled, so they are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A ship rescues fifty people at sea near a Caribbean port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port of Spain' is the capital of Trinidad, but here it is just a port in Spain. 'off' jumbles L and OCEAN into CELONA.
explanation.definitionFit: This Catalan city is a major Mediterranean seaport in Spain.

clue.text: Bark of a golden retriever

parts.note: a bark is a ship, and the golden retriever is the hero who sailed to bring back the Golden Fleece

explanation.surface: A dog's woof.
explanation.walkthrough: Bark (or barque) is a sailing ship; Jason retrieved the Golden Fleece in it, so the dog is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason's ship carried him and his crew on the quest for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Conclusions reached by bench are judicial and considered

indicators.note: the conclusions of words are their last letters

explanation.surface: A court's findings are both judicial and well weighed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be held to be something is to be regarded or judged as such.

clue.text: Grey makes a start (as horses do)

parts.note: to shy is to start or jump aside in fright, as a horse does

explanation.surface: A grey horse gives a jump of fright.
explanation.walkthrough: Grey looks like a horse's colour, but it is the definition. 'makes' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash-coloured, pale and greyish like cinders.

clue.text: State of Frenchman I walked back to guillotine, say

indicators.note: back says the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: etat is French for state
paced is walked step by step

explanation.surface: A French citizen marches backwards to the scaffold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ETAT + I + PACED as one run, giving DECAPI + TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead someone is what the guillotine does, as one example of the method.

clue.text: Man's house with lots of skeletons

explanation.surface: A Manxman's home with many skeletons in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man's parliament has a lower chamber called the House of ___; skeletons are master openers for locks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx parliament's lower chamber bears this name, and skeleton openers for locks are this kind of thing.

clue.text: Arranged neatly, we hear, on the rocks

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken, so a soundalike is entered

parts.note: to arrange neatly is to tidy, to put straight

explanation.surface: A neat arrangement, so they say, of drinks over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' looks like a drink with ice, but means financially in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of money, in reduced circumstances, is being in financial trouble.
